NDT training in Tacoma, WA: how it works for Tacoma employers and technicians

Short answer: NDT training for Tacoma employers and technicians is self-paced online theory with an ASNT NDT Level III answering questions, then hands-on practice in person at the employer's own yard, shop or plant. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Tacoma. The courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and the employer certifies its technicians. We reply within one business day.

Tacoma's economy is built on moving and making heavy things. Ships, containers, rail cars, structural steel, paper and metal products all pass through or are produced around Commencement Bay, and each of those activities needs steel that has been examined and documented. That gives the area steady demand for technicians who can do weld visual inspection, magnetic particle and penetrant testing, and ultrasonic thickness and weld work.

Waterfront work also changes how training should be planned. Marine and terminal steel is exposed to salt, moisture and weather, and many repair jobs happen on a vessel's schedule rather than a classroom's. Self-paced theory that can be studied at odd hours, followed by practical work at the employer's own yard, fits that reality better than a fixed timetable.

Request a Tacoma training quote, and tell us the methods, levels and head-count you have in mind. In Tacoma, anyone planning ahead can also read the NDT training FAQ, the Atlantis training overview and the USA training page.

How to get NDT certified in Tacoma: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

In Tacoma, certification in Washington follows the same pattern as elsewhere in the United States. In Tacoma, under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, the employer certifies its own technicians, and the standard is a set of recommended practices that each employer turns into a written practice of its own. Here is the sequence in order.

  1. Find or have an employer with a written practice. A technician in Tacoma is certified by the company that employs them, so the first step is a sponsor whose written practice covers the method and level you want. In Tacoma, the practice sets the hours, the examinations and the recertification interval.
  2. In Tacoma, complete the formal training. Take the classroom hours the written practice requires. The training-requirements matrix shows the SNT-TC-1A recommended hours for each method, and your Tacoma employer may set higher figures.
  3. Log supervised experience. Document the hours a Tacoma technician spends performing the method under a certified Level II or III. Experience is usually the slowest part for a new Tacoma technician, so start the log from the first day on a job.
  4. In Tacoma, pass the general examination on principles, equipment and terminology for the method.
  5. Pass the specific examination on the procedures, equipment and acceptance standards your Tacoma employer really uses.
  6. In Tacoma, pass the practical examination on real specimens, graded by a Level III or a qualified examiner working under one.
  7. In Tacoma, pass the vision examination: near-vision acuity and colour-contrast differentiation at the intervals the written practice sets. The SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker shows what to expect.
  8. Receive certification signed by your Tacoma employer.
  9. In Tacoma, recertify at the interval the written practice sets, which SNT-TC-1A recommends should not exceed five years, by examination or documented performance as permitted.

In Tacoma, ASNT central certification (ASNT 9712 for Level I and II, and ASNT NDT Level III examinations) is the alternative if you want a credential that stays with you rather than with an employer. Atlantis prepares candidates for that route too. See ASNT certification.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Tacoma technicians

In Tacoma, each course follows the body of knowledge in SNT-TC-1A for its method. In Tacoma, level 1 courses cover the fundamentals and working under supervision, Level 2 courses cover setting up, calibrating, performing and evaluating examinations to a procedure, and Level 3 preparation covers the basic and method examinations for those who will write procedures and examine others.

Method What the course covers Where it is used around Tacoma
UT Sound physics, calibration, thickness gauging, angle-beam weld examination, reporting Hull and tank thickness gauging in ship repair, weld checks on structural and pressure steel
RT In Tacoma, exposure technique, image quality, film and digital interpretation, radiation safety basics Pipe and pressure welds where specified; casting and fabrication checks
MT Magnetising methods, field direction, particle application, indication evaluation Structural welds, crane and terminal equipment, repair welds on vessels
PT Process control, dwell times, surface preparation, indication interpretation Stainless and non-magnetic piping, fittings, repair areas on marine systems
VT Acuity and lighting, weld profile, discontinuities, measuring tools, reporting First examination on almost every marine, terminal and structural job
PAUT Focal laws, encoded scanning, data analysis, sizing (UT Level II first) Thicker welds and corrosion mapping where the specification permits phased array
TOFD Diffraction technique, setup, flaw sizing (UT Level II first) Heavy-section welds in industrial and power equipment

In Tacoma, PAUT and TOFD are advanced ultrasonic techniques and are generally taken after UT Level II. In Tacoma, whether they can be used on a given job depends on the customer's specification and the employer's written practice.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Tacoma

Ultrasonic testing is the method that takes a Tacoma technician from surface checks to what is happening inside the steel. In ship repair and marine work the most common application is thickness gauging: measuring remaining wall on hull plating, tanks and piping so that owners and surveyors can see how much metal is left. Level I training covers the physics, equipment set-up, calibration and thickness readings. Level II adds angle-beam weld examination, evaluation against an acceptance standard and reporting.

Coating, scale and rough corrosion all make thickness gauging harder than it looks on a clean test block, and good technique on rough surfaces is something to practise deliberately. The Practical NDT simulator lets you rehearse set-ups and scanning patterns, and the ultrasonic testing training page shows what the course covers. For theory checks, try the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Where NDT technicians work around Tacoma

Ports and marine terminals. The Port of Tacoma runs container, bulk and breakbulk terminals, and the cranes, rail-mounted equipment, pilings and structures around them need regular inspection. Terminal owners set their own specifications, and the inspection mix is mostly visual and magnetic particle testing with ultrasonic thickness checks.

Ship repair and marine fabrication. Commencement Bay and Puget Sound support vessel repair, conversion and fabrication yards. Commercial vessels are generally inspected to classification society rules and U.S. Coast Guard requirements. Employers in this sector want technicians who can work to a written procedure on a moving schedule.

Military and defence. Joint Base Lewis-McChord, just south of the city, is one of the largest military installations on the West Coast, and the Puget Sound region has substantial Navy and Army maintenance activity. Defence contractors work to government specifications and their own quality programmes, and personnel requirements come from the contract. Atlantis training is based on SNT-TC-1A; whether it satisfies a particular contract is for the employer and its Level III to confirm.

Pulp, paper and process plants. Tacoma has long had pulp and paper manufacturing along its waterfront. Mills run boilers, digesters, tanks and piping that fall under ASME and National Board rules for in-service inspection, with ultrasonic thickness, visual and penetrant testing in regular use.

Steel, rail and construction. Rail yards, bridges, structural steel for commercial and public buildings, and metal fabricators across Pierce County all rely on AWS D1.1 and D1.5 inspection. That is a large steady source of VT and MT work for new technicians.

For earnings information on Tacoma-area work, see our NDT salary guide, which cites public sources. Multi-method technicians with current certifications generally have the widest choice of employers.

NDT schools and classes near Tacoma: what to compare

If you are looking for NDT schools or classes in Tacoma, you will see classroom programmes that run on a set timetable and self-paced options that put the theory online. A classroom can work well for someone between jobs who wants supervised time on specimens. Self-paced online theory works better for a technician already working on a vessel, a terminal or a shift pattern that does not leave room for scheduled evenings.

Compare providers on the points that decide whether the course will help you get work. Does a Level III teach and examine? Will the employer you are aiming for accept the training hours under its written practice? Does the provider claim to certify you, or does it say honestly that the employer certifies? For marine and defence work, ask whether the provider understands the customer requirements the employer must meet, because those can go beyond a general SNT-TC-1A course.

Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Tacoma. We offer online theory with Level III support, the Practical NDT simulator for rehearsal, and onsite practical examination at an employer's facility. Our near-me page explains how to approach employers about sponsorship.

Online NDT training in Washington

Technicians in Washington can complete Level I and II theory online at their own pace on the Atlantis portal, with Level III Q&A when a topic is unclear. Access opens the moment you enrol. A Tacoma technician on a yard schedule, or a terminal worker on rotating shifts, can study in short sessions. The hands-on training and practical examination take place in person at your employer's facility, and the employer certifies. See online NDT training and the Washington page.

Online theory covers the classroom portion only. In Tacoma, the Level III is available to answer questions while you study, and the portal opens the moment you enrol. In Tacoma, courses run year-round, so there is no fixed start date to wait for. Your employer's written practice still decides how many classroom hours count, which is why it helps to ask your Tacoma employer before you enrol.

Training a crew at your Tacoma facility

A Tacoma yard, fabricator or terminal contractor that needs to qualify several technicians can run the programme for the whole group: self-paced online theory so crews stay productive, followed by specific and practical examinations at your own facility on your own equipment and representative specimens. For marine employers the specific examination can use the acceptance criteria that apply on your vessels and structures.

If your written practice needs updating for new methods or customers, our Level III can help. See written practice development and corporate NDT training, or ask about training a Tacoma crew.

For Tacoma candidates the practical examination is hands-on with real equipment and specimens and is never conducted remotely. In Tacoma, if you want help writing the Level III side of the programme, see outsourced Level III consulting.

Radiography licensing in Washington

Washington is an NRC Agreement State. The Washington Department of Health licenses and inspects industrial radiography under its radioactive materials program, so a radiography company working in Tacoma needs the state's licence, and individual radiographers must meet the training and supervision conditions that licence sets. None of that comes from an RT method course. Atlantis RT training covers technique and interpretation under SNT-TC-1A and does not authorise anyone to use a source. Marine and terminal work also brings site-specific restrictions on exposure areas, so radiography schedules around active waterfront operations need planning with the owner. Check current requirements directly with the Department of Health.

Practise before your practical exam

The Practical NDT browser simulator lets a Tacoma technician rehearse set-ups, scanning coverage and interpretation in virtual workplaces between hands-on sessions, and the NDT practice tests cover the general and method theory. They are rehearsal tools. They do not replace hands-on training, logged experience or the practical examination on real specimens under your Tacoma employer's written practice.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Tacoma

How do I get NDT certified in Tacoma?

Work for, or be sponsored by, an employer that has an SNT-TC-1A written practice. You complete the required training and experience, pass general, specific and practical examinations and a vision test, and the employer certifies you. We provide the training and Level III support.

Is there NDT work in Tacoma for beginners?

Visual weld inspection and magnetic particle testing are common entry points around the port, shipyards and structural steel work. Check with local fabricators and repair contractors about their entry requirements.

Can I take NDT classes online in Washington?

The theory is available online and self-paced. Practical training and the practical examination are done hands-on with an employer.

What does ultrasonic thickness work involve in a shipyard?

A technician calibrates a gauge, takes readings across hull plate, tanks or piping, records them, and compares them with minimum thickness requirements. Surface condition and coatings affect technique.

How long is UT Level 2 training?

Your employer's written practice sets the hours. The training-requirements matrix lists SNT-TC-1A recommended hours, and experience usually takes longer than the classroom time.

Do military contractors accept SNT-TC-1A training?

Many do through the contractor's written practice, but the contract decides. Ask your employer's Level III which requirement applies before you plan your training.

Can I train as a Level III from Tacoma?

Yes, Level III preparation is online and self-paced with Level III Q&A. See ASNT Level III training for the examinations covered.

Does a course certificate make me certified?

No. Under SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies. The course is training and preparation. ASNT central certification is the route if you want a credential not tied to one employer.

Are there published fees for Tacoma courses?

Yes. The published US fees appear in the table on this page, and Register and Buy Now opens the course on the Atlantis portal.

Are there other training pages near Tacoma?

Yes. Nearby markets with their own guides include Seattle, Portland, Spokane, Anchorage, and the Washington training page covers the state as a whole.
